scenario: AITA for refusing to loan my brother my vacation money? | My (21F) brother (30M) and I live with our parents. He’s in a shitty job trying to get out so he went back to school and that’s why he moved back in 1 1/2 years ago. I’m in third year university and working to put myself through. I’m in business school which I am finding to difficult but not impossible. I should graduate in 2 years. When I got into uni I started saving for a bit of all my paycheques (whatever I could manage; sometimes it was as much as 15% and others as low as 1%) to go on a big vacation post uni gradation. Probably a cruise, Japan or a trip to different countries in Europe I’ve never been to. It has about $2800 in it now. My brother has not been on a vacation in many years and keeps hinting that he needs one. My parents already help him financially so he wouldn’t ask them for more help for that. Last week when he was complaining to my parents about it, they mentioned me and my vacation fund and said he could’ve been doing that all these years to be able to afford to go somewhere, or he could start now and maybe be able to go across country in a year. 3 days ago he came to me and asked if he could borrow my vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or Fall. He said since I won’t need it for another 2 years it’s plenty of time for him to pay me back. I said no. My brother is horrible with money. He makes about as much as I do yet always seems to be broke despite never buying groceries or paying rent (for the record, I do not pay rent either, which is why I have been able to build up the fund, but I do buy most of my own groceries, as well as pay for all my makeup, health supplies, phone and uni fees). He’s very mad I said no. He says it’s jor fair as the youngest child I got to go away with mom and dad more while he had to go to college or work because he had moved out and was older. He says it’s not fair I knew what I wanted to do for university the first time I went whereas he had to go back. He says I’ve only been able to save so much money because “mom and dad spoiled me.” I disagree. My father, as well as my uni accounting and finance classes taught me to budget. If anything I think my parents spoiled him Because doesn’t know how to do much of anything for the real world outside his actual job. I don’t think it’s fair for me to have to give up my vacation money to him. I doubt he will be able to pay me back in time. Even if he couldn’t roger he could... I’m uncomfortable. AITA?

The sister is 21 years old, in her third year of university, and working to pay for her education. She's in business school, which she finds challenging but manageable. She's been saving money from her paychecks for a big vacation after she graduates, which is in about two years. Her vacation fund has $2,800 in it, and she's planning to go on a cruise or visit places like Japan or Europe. Her brother is 30 years old, living with their parents, and is in a tough job while trying to go back to school to improve his situation. He's been living with their parents for about a year and a half. He hasn't been on a vacation in many years and has been hinting that he needs one. Their parents have been helping him financially, but he didn't ask them for more help for the vacation. Instead, they suggested that he could have been saving money like the sister did or start saving now to afford a trip within a year. Three days ago, the brother approached the sister and asked to borrow her vacation money to go on a trip to Japan this summer or fall. He argued that since she won't need the money for another two years, he would have plenty of time to pay her back. The sister refused, citing her brother's poor money management skills and her own need for the money for her future vacation. The brother is upset and feels it's unfair that the sister gets to go on more trips with their parents while he had to work or go to college. He also points out that the sister knew what she wanted to do for university from the start, unlike him, and that her ability to save money is because "mom and dad spoiled her." The sister disagrees, stating that her parents taught her to budget and that her brother doesn't know how to manage money or handle real-world situations outside his job. The sister feels it's unfair to give up her vacation money to her brother, especially since she doubts he'll be able to pay her back in time. She's uncomfortable with the situation and is asking if she's acting inappropriately (AITA). Alright, so I need to determine whether it's right or wrong for the sister to refuse the loan. Let's break this down. First, the sister has been saving money for her future vacation, which is a significant goal for her. She's been working and budgeting to achieve this, which shows responsibility and foresight. Her brother, on the other hand, has a history of poor money management, as indicated by his current financial situation despite earning a similar income to his sister. He's also been living with their parents, which might have contributed to his financial dependency. The sister's refusal to lend her brother the money can be seen from a few perspectives: 1. **Financial Responsibility:** The sister is responsible with her money, as evidenced by her savings. Lending money to someone who has shown poor money management skills could put her own financial goals at risk. If her brother is unable to pay back the loan, she could lose the money intended for her vacation, which is a significant personal goal. 2. **Family Dynamics:** The sister feels that her brother is making unfair comparisons about their childhood experiences and the support they've received from their parents. She believes that her ability to save is due to her own efforts and the lessons she's learned from her parents, not because of being "spoiled." This adds emotional weight to her refusal, as she feels her brother is not acknowledging her hard work and financial discipline. 3. **Potential for Conflict:** Agreeing to lend the money could lead to further conflict if the brother is unable to repay the loan. This could strain their already tense relationship, especially given the brother's resentment towards the sister for what he perceives as unfair treatment. 4. **Alternative Solutions:** Instead of borrowing money, the sister could suggest other ways for her brother to save for his vacation, such as creating a budget, cutting unnecessary expenses, or seeking additional income. This approach would empower her brother to take control of his finances without jeopardizing her own goals. 5. **Ethical Considerations:** While it's important to support family members, it's also crucial to set boundaries to protect one's own financial well-being. The sister's refusal can be seen as a responsible decision to prioritize her future goals over her brother's immediate desires, especially given his history of poor financial management. In conclusion, the sister's decision to refuse the loan appears to be a responsible and reasonable choice, considering her financial goals, her brother's money management skills, and the potential for conflict. It's important for her to communicate her reasons clearly to her brother to avoid misunderstandings and to maintain a respectful relationship.
